title: acme-orders: where a missing test hurts most
subtitle: Which code to test first, the cases no test covers with their expected results, and what the existing tests miss.

verdict.text: Test `src/acme_orders/importer.py` first. A test for decimal commas (`12,50`) was deleted in `49bc16d`, the real export uses them, and the production log shows the nightly import exiting with `decimal.InvalidOperation` at `importer.py:28` since 2026-10-02 [high]. Next is `report.py`: no tests, and it has three likely bugs in the finance report [med].

stats.label: Untested files
stats.note: no test file names them; no coverage report

blocks.text: The repo has no coverage report (no coverage.py JSON, Cobertura or lcov). The ranking uses the weaker signal "a test file names the module". This overstates `importer.py` and `pricing.py`: both are named, but the decimal-comma path and `STAFF25` have no test. It also counts `__init__`/`__main__` as tested only because the tests import the package.

items: `unittest`, as in CI: `PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests`
180 days before the last commit (13 commits, 2026-05-04 → 2026-10-03)
risk × change rate × gap × size, from `gaps.py`; my re-ranking is in the next section

`logs/acme-orders.log`: I read only the error and cron lines, with e-mail addresses masked. `data/`: I read only the headers, plus counts of which values contain a comma. No row content went into this page or into any test.
Run `coverage run -m unittest discover -s tests && coverage json`, then re-rank with `--coverage coverage.json` (not run yet: waiting for your yes).

sections.title: Ranking
sections.intro: Script rank and score next to my rank after reading the code. I confirmed each risk family against the code, and the 'why' column says what moved a file.

rows: **Moved up 4.** Every total starts here. `49bc16d` removed decimal-comma parsing and its test. The real export has commas in 2 of 8 rows, and the log shows the import exiting 1 on 2026-10-02 and 2026-10-03 [high].

**Moved up 1.** Finance reads it, and it has no tests. It sums every row of the monthly adjustments file whatever the `day` column says. It shows discount and VAT unrounded since `7a9f245`. It renders CSV values into HTML with autoescape off. Its adjustment parser also rejects decimal commas, and one of the two real adjustment rows has one [med].

**Moved down 1.** `total_cents` is finance's contract (`docs/finance-export.md`), and nothing tests it. The code is simple, though, and changed once. `totals_by_day` is called nowhere in `src` [high].

**Moved up 3.** It is the core money logic and changes often. `STAFF25` shipped without a test, no test covers the half-up rounding boundary, and the `ACME_VAT_RATE` setting is ignored (hard-coded `0.20`) [high].
outside calls (via notify); money hit is only a call to `order_total`

**Moved down 4.** Its churn comes from adding a subcommand five times, and the dispatch is glue. One real risk: `import --notify` sends a receipt for every order on every run, so a re-import re-sends them. One failed send also stops the rest [high].
**Moved down 2.** The `money` hits are `vat_rate`, which nothing reads. Env-over-YAML precedence has no test. `yaml.load(FullLoader)` with PyYAML 5.3.1 belongs to dependency-audit [med].
Sends e-mail to customers. `requests.post` has no timeout, so the import can hang [high]. It is small (11 lines).

**Moved down 2.** It is read-only, and the `money` hit is only `cents / 100`. A query string is treated as part of the order id. It has no auth and binds `0.0.0.0` while serving customer e-mails: that is a security question, not a test gap [med].
Dropped: two lines each, nothing to test.

items.title: Deleted test `test_decimal_comma` covered a case production still sends
items.evidence: `49bc16d` "importer: simplify amount parsing" changed `parse_amount` from `Decimal(value.strip().replace(",", "."))` to `Decimal(value.strip())` and deleted `assertEqual(parse_amount("12,50"), Decimal("12.50"))`. In `data/orders-2026-10-02.csv`, 2 of 8 `unit_price` values contain a comma. `logs/acme-orders.log` shows the first cron run after the deploy of `c376ea1` exiting 1 with `decimal.InvalidOperation` at `importer.py:28`, on 2026-10-02 and again on 2026-10-03. The run on 2026-10-01 (deployed `d22ee8f`) imported 37 orders [high].
items.fix: Restore the test as a regression test (first tests, step 1). It will fail today, so the fix goes to bug-hunt. Finance's `total_cents` has probably been missing orders since 2026-10-02: check that the production import is still failing [med].

items.title: Three behaviour changes shipped without a test
items.evidence: `d22ee8f` added the `STAFF25` discount with no test. `c376ea1` added the adjustments file to the report with no test. `7a9f245` moved rounding from `vat_total` to `order_total`; it tested the total but not the report, which still prints `vat_total` and `discount_total` unrounded [high].
items.fix: Covered by the first tests below (pricing and report).

items.title: No empty, skipped or mock-only tests
items.evidence: All 7 tests assert real values on real objects. None are skipped, none are marked expected-to-fail, and none use mocks. The script's count agrees with my reading [high]. They cover only the happy path: no test feeds bad input.
items.fix: None needed: the gap is in what the tests cover, not in how they assert.

sections.title: First tests
sections.intro: Four steps, highest value for the effort first. All are `unittest`, matching the repo's tests and CI. The data is made up; nothing comes from `data/`. I will write and run them after your yes, and leave the **Question** cases out until they are answered.

items.title: 1. Restore the decimal-comma regression test
items.text: `ParseAmountTest.test_decimal_comma`: `parse_amount("12,50")` → `Decimal("12.50")`. `ReadOrdersTest.test_decimal_comma_in_export`: made-up row with `4,50` × 2 → line `Decimal("4.50")`, `order_total` `10.80`. **Both fail today.** That failure is the bug: I will hand it to bug-hunt, not soften the expectation.

items.title: 2. New report tests
items.text: With 2 made-up adjustment rows (10-01: `-5.00`, 10-02: `7.00`) and `day=2026-10-01`, the report shows `Adjustments: -5.00`. A `-12,50` amount reads as `-12.50`. An order_id `A-1` comes out escaped. Each of these three is expected to fail today. Only the empty-input case (`Adjustments: 0`) should pass. The day filter needs a quick yes from finance first. Jinja2 is not installed in the local Python, so these tests need the project's dependencies installed first.

items.title: 3. New storage tests
items.text: These run against `sqlite3` `:memory:`. Round trip gives `total_cents` `1080`. `0.29` gives `29`. A re-save with fewer lines leaves 1 order row and 1 line. An unknown id gives `None`. All should pass today; they guard finance's contract.

items.title: 4. Pricing gaps
items.text: `STAFF25` on `10.00` gives `9.00`. The half-up boundary, `1.45` with `STAFF25`, gives `1.31`. Lower-case `staff25` gives `9.00`. An empty order gives `0.00`. All should pass today.

blocks.text: Questions to settle before they become tests: report VAT/discount rounding and the day filter, a discount code on a later line, timestamps without an offset, `ACME_VAT_RATE`, and re-sent receipts. Finance owns `total_cents` (docs/finance-export.md).
